articles.title: Jenny McCarthy’s Son Posts Tearful Message About Having to Leave Childhood Home After Sale, Vows to Buy It Back Someday
articles.summary: “I have officially moved away from my home and life just won’t be the same anymore,” Evan Asher said on Instagram, where his mom and stepdad Donnie Wahlberg...
articles.body:
Jenny McCarthy's son Evan Joseph Asher, said leaving his childhood home was "the saddest moment of my entire life"

In a video shared to Instagram, the content creator, 24, wipes away tears as he vows to someday buy back the Illinois mansion

Asher's mom and stepdad Donnie Wahlberg wrote sweet messages of support in the comments as they start their new chapter in Las Vegas

Jenny McCarthy 's son is saying a tearful goodbye to his childhood home.

The Masked Singer judge, 54, and her husband, New Kids on the Block singer Donnie Wahlberg , 57, sold their Tudor-style mansion in St. Charles, Ill., for $2.65 million, according to property records.

While McCarthy previously confirmed that the family would be starting a new chapter in Las Vegas , her son Evan Asher , a 24-year-old content creator and YouTuber, deemed the day he had to leave his childhood home "the saddest moment of my entire life."

"I have officially moved away from my home and life just won't be the same anymore," Evan, whom McCarthy shares with ex John Asher, wrote on Instagram alongside a video of himself wiping away tears. "I'm so sorry, I was very emotional. But when you live somewhere most of your life, have so many friends, and make more nostalgic memories than everything in any other house that you've lived in it's a lot to take in."

"I knew I had to share my emotions with you all," he continued. "This house has done so much for me over the past 11 years and I hope it will do it for the new owners too. One day. ONE DAY. I will buy this place again and start a family of my own. Thank you house for everything overall. I love you and god bless you."

In the video, Evan, who has more than 67,000 followers across his Instagram and TikTok , admitted that he wasn't "doing so great" after moving out of the house he lived in for so many years.

"It doesn't feel the same anymore when someone else owns the place because you're not living there anymore," he said through tears. "It just really hurts. It hurts really bad. I'm just not doing great."

"I'm just gonna miss all the times I had there," he added. "I'm happy, though, for my parents. They made the right decision. But at the same time, it's just still so hard. But I'll be okay, we'll be okay."

In the comments of Evan's post, both his mom and stepdad shared messages of support.

"Promise someday you're gonna knock on that door and buy it for your family," McCarthy wrote. "It's not goodbye. It's see you later. I love you. Hugging and kissing your heart. ❤️ 🙏🏻"

Wahlberg added, "I love you Evan. Glad we got to cry together last weekend. 😢."

articles.title: Grupo de percussão de Salvador participa de festival no Equador | G1
articles.standfirst: Cinco integrantes do Repiquesia, projeto sociocultural criado no bairro da Federação, participaram de oficinas e atividades culturais em duas cidades equatorianas.
articles.summary: Cinco integrantes do Repiquesia, projeto sociocultural criado no bairro da Federação, participaram de oficinas e atividades culturais em duas cidades equatorianas.
articles.body:
Grupo de percussão Repiquesia — Foto: Divulgação

Cinco integrantes do grupo sociocultural Repiquesia, criado no bairro da Federação, em Salvador , participaram de um intercâmbio cultural no Equador, entre os dias 12 e 16 de novembro. Durante a viagem, os músicos compartilharam ritmos afro-baianos e participaram de atividades de formação artística.

Criado em 2013 por Geraldo Marques e Thamara Ferreira, o Repiquesia oferece formação musical gratuita para crianças, jovens e adultos, principalmente moradores de comunidades periféricas de Salvador.

A programação aconteceu nas cidades de Jipijapa e Calceta, na província de Manabí, a convite do grupo equatoriano Los Inocencios.

Os participantes realizaram oficinas de percussão afro-baiana, trocaram experiências com artistas locais e participaram do Festival Afro Montuvio, dedicado à valorização das manifestações culturais afro-latino-americanas.

O grupo já participou de intercâmbios culturais em países como Argentina, Japão, Espanha, Canadá, Uruguai, além de Hong Kong e Taiwan.

Após a experiência no Equador, o projeto prevê a realização de uma atividade gratuita em Salvador, chamada “Roda Aberta – Vivências do Tambor”.

O encontro será aberto ao público e terá compartilhamento das experiências adquiridas durante a viagem, além de atividades de percussão. A data não foi detalhada.

articles.title: São Paulo tem o maior número de mortes no trânsito em 10 anos; pedestres e motociclistas são as principais vítimas | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento mostra que 410 motociclistas e 332 pedestres morreram em acidentes na capital em 2026. Especialistas apontam avanço de motos no sinal vermelho e tempo insuficiente para travessias como fatores de risco.
articles.summary: Levantamento mostra que 410 motociclistas e 332 pedestres morreram em acidentes na capital em 2026. Especialistas apontam avanço de motos no sinal vermelho e tempo insuficiente para travessias como fatores de risco.
articles.body:
A cidade de São Paulo registrou 867 mortes no trânsito entre janeiro e outubro de 2026. É o maior número para o período em dez anos , segundo levantamento feito com dados do Infosiga. Motociclistas e pedestres concentram a maior parte das vítimas, em um cenário de aumento dos acidentes fatais na capital.

Do total de mortes, 410 foram de motociclistas e 332 de pedestres . O número de pedestres mortos é o segundo maior da série histórica.

Enquanto os índices de mortes no trânsito apresentam queda no estado de São Paulo, na capital a tendência é oposta: os registros continuam aumentando.

Um dos problemas apontados por especialistas é o desrespeito aos semáforos por motociclistas, que avançam mesmo quando o sinal está vermelho. A situação coloca em risco principalmente quem atravessa as ruas a pé.

Em um cruzamento da Avenida 9 de Julho com a Avenida Brasil, na Zona Oeste da capital, uma equipe de reportagem acompanhou a espera de pedestres para atravessar.

Duas mulheres aguardavam a abertura do semáforo na chuva havia pelo menos 8 minutos. Mesmo depois de apertarem o botão para solicitar a travessia, o sinal continuava fechado (veja abaixo) . Elas conseguiram atravessar após 13 minutos de espera no total.

Pedestres estavam há 8 minutos aguardando para atravessar avenida de SP e conseguiram percorrer trajeto após 13 minutos de espera — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo especialistas em segurança viária, a demora pode levar pedestres a tentar atravessar em momentos inadequados, aumentando o risco de atropelamentos.

Historicamente, os automóveis são os principais responsáveis pelas mortes de pedestres em acidentes de trânsito. Mas essa proporção vem mudando, com participação cada vez maior das motocicletas.

O especialista em segurança viária Diogo Dias afirma que o avanço de motociclistas no sinal vermelho tem se tornado mais frequente.

"É possível afirmar empiricamente que sim. O avanço ao sinal vermelho tem aumentado cada vez mais, principalmente por parte das motocicletas. E isso coloca em risco, principalmente os pedestres", explicou.

Segundo ele, o pedestre fica especialmente vulnerável quando recebe autorização para atravessar, mas encontra motocicletas avançando de diferentes direções.

Mortes de pedestres provocadas por motos aumentam

Os dados do Infosiga mostram o crescimento da participação das motocicletas nos atropelamentos fatais.

Em 2023, as motos foram responsáveis por 19% das mortes de pedestres, enquanto os automóveis responderam por 44%. No ano seguinte, a participação das motocicletas subiu para 24%, e a dos carros caiu para 39%.

Em 2025, as motos já representavam 27% das mortes de pedestres. Entre 2021 e 2025, a participação dos motociclistas nesse tipo de ocorrência aumentou sete pontos percentuais.

Diogo Dias explica que os conflitos entre motociclistas e pedestres não acontecem apenas durante a madrugada, período em que são registradas mais ocorrências fatais. Eles também são comuns nos horários de pico, quando as motos circulam pelos corredores entre os carros.

Nessas situações, os pedestres podem não perceber a aproximação das motocicletas. O risco aumenta tanto quando alguém atravessa fora da faixa ou em um momento inadequado quando o motociclista desrespeita o sinal.

Mortes no trânsito de São Paulo chegam a 867 até outubro, maior número em dez anos — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Tempo dos semáforos prioriza fluidez do trânsito, diz especialista

Para quem circula a pé pela capital, atravessar algumas vias pode se transformar em uma longa espera.

A arquiteta e especialista em mobilidade Meli Malatesta, integrante da ONG Cidade a Pé, chama a atenção para a programação dos semáforos. Segundo ela, os tempos de abertura e fechamento são definidos para favorecer a fluidez dos veículos, e não necessariamente para garantir mais segurança aos pedestres.

Para demonstrar o problema, ela gravou um vídeo em uma esquina da Avenida Rebouças com a Rua Oscar Freire. Nas imagens, mostra que o tempo em que o sinal permanece fechado para quem está a pé é suficiente para preparar um prato de macarrão instantâneo (assista abaixo) .

Meli afirma que já existem recursos tecnológicos capazes de ajudar a reduzir os riscos, mas que a adoção dessas medidas depende de decisões do poder público.

"Acho que hoje a tecnologia, investimento em tecnologia permite tudo, mas tem que ter vontade política, né? Antes de tudo, para se investir em medidas que diminuam essas tragédias", afirmou.

"Cada morte, pessoa que morre em um acidente de trânsito não é só um número, é uma tragédia numa família, numa comunidade. Então os tomadores de decisão têm que ter consciência disso", completou.

Tempo de espera para abrir semáforo em SP é o mesmo para cozinhar macarrão instantâneo — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Em nota, a Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET) informou que realiza ações contínuas para ampliar a segurança no sistema viário da capital.

Entre as principais iniciativas, a companhia destacou a Faixa Azul, destinada à circulação de motociclistas.

Para proteger os pedestres, a CET citou a implantação de áreas calmas, onde a velocidade máxima permitida é de 30 km/h, as Rotas Escolares Seguras, a ampliação do tempo de travessia nas faixas de pedestres e a construção de travessias elevadas.

articles.title: Arturo Pérez-Reverte: "Vox es como el Partido Popular con cuatro copas"
articles.standfirst: El escritor ha sido el invitado de Pablo Motos este miércoles en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.summary: El escritor ha sido el invitado de Pablo Motos este miércoles en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.body: El escritor Arturo Pérez-Reverte ha visitado este miércoles 'El Hormiguero' para presentar su nueva novela, 'La hipótesis más peligrosa', y conversar con Pablo Motos sobre algunos asuntos de actualidad como la situación política española, el atractivo de la derecha entre los votantes jóvenes y el desencanto de una parte de la ciudadanía con sus representantes políticos. Durante la entrevista, ha compartido también algunas valoraciones personales sobre Pedro Sánchez, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, Santiago Abascal, Ada Colau, Gabriel Rufián y Pablo Iglesias. Una de las declaraciones más llamativas ha llegado al hablar del respaldo electoral al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez. "Conozco gente que lo odia y lo va a votar", ha asegurado Pérez-Reverte. El escritor ha precisado que no se refería a personas sin criterio: "No hablo de tarugos, hablo de gente de nivel". Preguntado por Pablo Motos sobre cómo explica esa aparente contradicción, ha respondido: "Porque España es un país enfermo". El autor ha relacionado esta reflexión con distintos episodios de la historia política española. "Es una enfermedad que hizo que nos cargáramos la Primera República, la Restauración, la Segunda República, nos estamos cargando la Transición: España es un país enfermo", ha afirmado. No obstante, ha preferido no extenderse en el análisis y ha optado por la prudencia para evitar seguir dando titulares. La conversación también ha abordado el atractivo de la derecha entre los votantes más jóvenes. A raíz de una pregunta sobre qué partido podría votar el protagonista adolescente de su nueva novela, Pérez-Reverte ha ofrecido una comparación entre los principales referentes del Partido Popular (PP) y Vox. "Para los jóvenes creo, bueno, está probado, entre los jóvenes hasta los 40 años lo que está de moda es la derecha", ha señalado. A continuación, ha descrito a Alberto Núñez Feijóo como "el padre aburrido que te da el sermón", mientras que ha presentado a Santiago Abascal como "el tío golfo, el tío que no es fiable, que te da tabaco, que te deja conducir el coche, que te lleva a tomar una copa". De esta comparación ha surgido una de las frases más comentadas de la entrevista: "Vox es como el PP con cuatro copas". El escritor también ha expresado sus reservas sobre el líder de la formación y sus propuestas electorales, al considerar que "promete cosas que saben que no podrán cumplir". Pérez-Reverte también ha comentado la trayectoria de otros representantes políticos. Sobre Ada Colau, ha recurrido a una comparación muy gráfica: "Es como una cena recalentada". En cambio, ha tenido palabras favorables para Gabriel Rufián, de quien ha destacado su capacidad para conectar con los jóvenes, su desenvoltura y sus habilidades parlamentarias. Al mencionar a los políticos que considera mejores parlamentarios, ha citado al portavoz de ERC junto a Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo y Félix Bolaños. Su valoración de Pablo Iglesias ha sido más crítica. "Realmente no es un político, es un buscavidas porque está deseando hacer fondo", ha comentado durante la entrevista. Más allá de las valoraciones sobre dirigentes y partidos, Pérez-Reverte ha dedicado una parte de la entrevista a reflexionar sobre el estado de ánimo de los ciudadanos ante las próximas elecciones generales del 29-N. Para el escritor, uno de los principales problemas es la pérdida de confianza en la clase política y la dificultad para encontrar motivos para el optimismo. "La falta de fe nos está produciendo una especie de descorazonamiento, ya no creemos en los políticos", ha explicado. En su opinión, las sucesivas decepciones han provocado que muchos ciudadanos hayan dejado de confiar en las soluciones que ofrecen sus representantes y se conformen con elegir "la hipótesis menos mala". El escritor ha insistido en que esta desconfianza no se limita a una formación política concreta, sino que responde a una acumulación de promesas incumplidas y decepciones. "Nos han engañado tantas veces, nos han defraudado tantas veces, unos y otros, aunque últimamente nos está mintiendo el mismo, que lo peor es la falta de esperanza", ha concluido.

articles.title: Marina Sena, Roberto Menescal, Danilo Caymmi, Luísa Sonza e espetáculo 'Uma Noite com os Bee Gees' animam fim de semana no DF | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação também conta com Festa A Volta aos Anos 80, stand-up com grupo 4 Amigos e 22ª Mostra de Cinema Europeu. Veja o que fazer no Distrito Federal entre quinta-feira (19) e domingo (22).
articles.summary: Programação também conta com Festa A Volta aos Anos 80, stand-up com grupo 4 Amigos e 22ª Mostra de Cinema Europeu. Veja o que fazer no Distrito Federal entre quinta-feira (19) e domingo (22).
articles.body:
Marina Sena se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Anderson Bordê/AgNews

O fim de semana vai começar mais cedo, em razão do feriado desta sexta-feira (20), e os moradores do Distrito Federal já tem opções para se divertir desde esta quinta-feira (19).

Um dos destaques da programação é o show "Coisas Naturais" de Marina Sena, nesta quinta, no Festival Estilo Brasil, no Ulysses Centro de Convenções. No domingo (22), o festival traz Roberto Menescal com Danilo Caymmi, Patty Ascher e participação especial de Luísa Sonza.

Também nesta quinta-feira, a banda argentina Geminis, dedicada há mais de 25 anos à obra dos Bee Gees, apresenta o espetáculo "Uma Noite com os Bee Gees", e pela primeira vez no Brasil, o tributo será apresentado com orquestra ao vivo.

A programação também conta com Festa A Volta aos Anos 80, stand-up com grupo 4 Amigos e 22ª Mostra de Cinema Europeu. Veja o que fazer no Distrito Federal entre quinta-feira (19) e domingo (22):

Marina Sena traz a turnê Coisas Naturais à Brasília

Roberto Menescal faz show com Danilo Caymmi, Patty Ascher e participação especial de Luísa Sonza

'Uma Noite com os Bee Gees' em versão sinfônica

Rincon Sapiência se apresenta no Teatro Newton Rossi

Espetáculo 'Eu Quero Ser Uma Locomotiva' em Brasília

Michel Alcoforado com 'Coisa de Rico: Outras Histórias'

Tributo a Michael Jackson inspirado na Bad Tour 1987 no Teatro Brasília Shopping

Orquestra de Bandolins de Brasília celebra 200 anos do instrumento na Infinu

22ª Mostra de Cinema Europeu traz 14 filmes gratuitos para o Cine Brasília

Dupla Alex Matos & Luciano lança videoclipe no Sesc de Ceilândia

Marina Sena chega ao palco do Festival Estilo Brasil, nesta quinta-feira (19), com a turnê Coisas Naturais, inspirada no terceiro álbum de sua carreira. Em uma apresentação que combina música, performance e elementos teatrais, a cantora explora uma fase artística marcada pela intensidade, pela liberdade de expressão e por uma relação mais direta entre o que acontece no palco e o público.

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 126,65, pelo site

Neste domingo (22), Roberto Menescal se apresenta no Festival Estilo Brasil com o show "Bossa Sempre Nova". Ao lado de Danilo Caymmi e Patty Ascher, Menescal apresenta um repertório que atravessa décadas da música brasileira, com participação especial de Luísa Sonza.

O repertório preparado para Brasília percorre diferentes momentos da música brasileira. Patty Ascher interpreta clássicos como "Chega de Saudade", "Desafinado", "Wave" e "Dindi", enquanto Danilo Caymmi apresenta canções como "A Felicidade", "Samba do Avião" e "Andança".

A participação especial de Luísa Sonza acontece na parte final do espetáculo. A cantora interpreta músicas como "Chico", "Você" e "Samba de Verão", antes de se juntar aos demais artistas em clássicos como "O Barquinho" e "Garota de Ipanema", que encerram o encontro.

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 67,15, pelo site

Geminis Bee Gees Tribute — Foto: Divulgação

Um dos repertórios mais conhecidos da música pop mundial ganha versão sinfônica em Brasília. Nesta quinta-feira (19), a banda argentina Geminis, dedicada há mais de 25 anos à obra dos Bee Gees, apresenta o espetáculo "Uma Noite com os Bee Gees", pela primeira vez no Brasil, o tributo será apresentado com orquestra ao vivo.

Com cerca de duas horas de duração, o espetáculo passeia por diferentes fases dos Bee Gees e reúne os grandes sucessos que atravessaram gerações, além de composições dos irmãos Gibb gravadas por artistas como Barbra Streisand, Dionne Warwick, Kenny Rogers, Frankie Valli e Celine Dion. O repertório traz ainda uma homenagem a Andy Gibb, irmão mais novo do trio, e canções que nunca chegaram a ser apresentadas ao vivo pelos Bee Gees.

📍 Local: Auditório Planalto — Centro de Convenções Ulysses Guimarães

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 140, pelo site

Nesta sexta-feira (20), a Festa A Volta aos Anos 80 está de volta a Brasília com muita nostalgia, música e clássicos que marcaram gerações. A nova edição promete muita animação, clássicos dos anos 80 e uma experiência pensada para quem quer reviver uma das décadas mais marcantes da música e da cultura pop, com show da banda Distintos Filhos e Dado Villa-Lobos.

📍 Local: Temporâneo – Salão A – AABB – St. de Clubes Sul

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 70, pelo site

4 Amigos – A Banca de Piadas será em Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Acervo @os4amigos

Neste sábado (21), o grupo 4 Amigos está de volta à Brasília, em um espetáculo totalmente inédito com uma sessão extra, preservando a essência do stand-up comedy que consagrou o grupo pelo país. No palco, Dihh Lopes, Thiago Ventura, Afonso Padilha e Márcio Donato apresentam novas histórias, textos afiados e observações do cotidiano, mantendo o humor direto, autoral e sem filtro que define o verdadeiro stand-up.

Entre os momentos inéditos do espetáculo, destaque para o novo quadro Coletiva de Imprensa, em que os integrantes encaram perguntas e situações inesperadas em uma dinâmica leve, caótica e extremamente divertida, explorando o improviso e a personalidade única de cada comediante.

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 90, pelo site

Nesta sexta-feira (20), Rincon Sapiência se apresenta no Teatro Newton Rossi. Reconhecido nacionalmente por sua contribuição ao rap brasileiro, o artista leva ao palco uma produção musical marcada pela valorização da identidade negra e pela conexão entre ritmos contemporâneos e referências afro-brasileiras.

📍 Local: Teatro Newton Rossi – Sesc Ceilândia

🎫 Entrada gratuita, distribuída na bilheteria do teatro duas horas antes do evento

Nesta quinta-feira (19), o espetáculo Eu Quero Ser Uma Locomotiva, da Cia Pierrot Lunar, chega ao Teatro do CCBB Brasília. A montagem reúne teatro, música e objetos antigos para refletir sobre memória, envelhecimento e reinvenção depois dos 50 anos. Em cena, Neise Neves e Léo Quintão interpretam dois algoritmos do futuro que revisitam suas experiências em uma cápsula à deriva.

🗓️ Quando: quinta-feira (19) até 6 de dezembro

⏰ Horário: quinta-feira a sábado, às 20h, e domingos, às 18h30

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 15, pelo site

Michel Alcoforado estreia o especial de teatro "Coisa de Rico: Outras Histórias" em São Paulo — Foto: Luiza Sigulem

Michel Alcoforado chega a Brasília neste sábado (21), com a aula-espetáculo "Coisa de Rico: Outras Histórias".

O espetáculo combina antropologia, humor e histórias do cotidiano para discutir riqueza, desigualdade, comportamento e os códigos sociais que atravessam a vida dos brasileiros. Ao longo de aproximadamente 80 minutos, Michel transforma pesquisas, conceitos e observações acumulados em sua trajetória em uma experiência que aproxima o conhecimento antropológico do público.

📍 Local: Auditório Planalto do Ulysses Centro de Convenções

O cantor e instrumentista Gigio Teixeira sobe ao palco do Clube do Choro de Brasília, nesta quinta-feira (19), com o espetáculo "Country Heroes", fazendo uma verdadeira viagem sonora pelos grandes clássicos e ícones da country music. articles.standfirst: Evento vai de 19 a 25 de novembro, com atividades gratuitas em Maceió e em União dos Palmares.
articles.summary: O festival Vamos Subir a Serra celebra a resistência negra com shows de Ilê Aiyê e Tatau, feiras e oficinas gratuitas em Maceió e na histórica Serra da Barriga.
articles.body:
Vamos Subir a Serra chega à 10ª edição em 2025 — Foto: Divulgação/Vamos Subir a Serra

O mês de novembro é marcado por atividades que celebram a cultura, a história e a resistência da população negra no Brasil. Em Alagoas, um dos eventos que integram essa programação é o festival Vamos Subir a Serra, que chega à 10ª edição entre os dias 19 e 25 de novembro.

A ação conta com mais de 60 atividades gratuitas em Maceió e na Serra da Barriga, em União dos Palmares , local que simboliza a resistência do Quilombo dos Palmares (veja a programação abaixo) .

Realizado desde 2017 pelo Centro de Cultura e Estudos Étnicos Anajô, entidade ligada ao movimento negro alagoano, o festival reúne manifestações artísticas, debates, literatura, gastronomia e iniciativas de valorização da identidade afro-brasileira.

A proposta é conectar a capital alagoana ao território histórico do Quilombo dos Palmares, levando ao público experiências culturais e educativas relacionadas à memória da população negra e à luta contra o racismo.

Entre os destaques da programação estão as apresentações musicais do grupo Ilê Aiyê, de Tatau e de Tiganá Santana . O festival também promove encontros literários com as escritoras Cida Bento e Carla Akotirene , além de oficinas infantis e atividades voltadas à cultura digital.

Vamos Subir a Serra tem programação entre 19 e 25 de novembro, em Maceió e União dos Palmares — Foto: Divulgação/Vamos Subir a Serra

A primeira etapa do festival acontece na Praia de Pajuçara, entre quinta-feira (19) e domingo (22), das 12h às 22h. O espaço será dividido em quatro áreas integradas, com atividades culturais, esportivas e de incentivo à economia criativa.

Uma das novidades desta edição é a 1ª Corrida Palmares Vive , marcada para o feriado de 20 de novembro, Dia Nacional de Zumbi e da Consciência Negra.

A programação também inclui feiras de afroempreendedorismo e gastronomia, com 150 expositores, que vão apresentar produtos, artesanato, moda e pratos da culinária afro-brasileira e regional.

Outra atração é a Oca Afrofuturo, espaço de cultura digital que utilizará óculos de realidade virtual para proporcionar aos visitantes uma experiência imersiva no Parque Memorial Quilombo dos Palmares.

O evento terá ainda o Festival Nacional de Hip-Hop e o Seminário da Política Nacional de Equidade, Educação para as Relações Étnico-Raciais e Educação Escolar Quilombola (PNEERQ), realizado em parceria com o Ministério da Educação (MEC).

Festival Vamos Subir a Serra conta com programação na Serra da Barriga, em União dos Palmares — Foto: Divulgação/Vamos Subir a Serra

A partir de 23 de novembro, o festival sobe a Serra da Barriga, em União dos Palmares e realiza atividades no Parque Memorial. Entre as ações estão a vivência Palmares In Loco, o Festival Nacional de Hip-Hop – Batalha de Palmares e um seminário.

O encerramento, na noite de 25 de novembro, conta com uma intervenção de projeção mapeada no platô da Serra da Barriga, coroada por uma tradicional gira de samba de caboclo.

Quinta-feira (19): Abertura oficial com a energia contagiante do Rock Maracatu, o tradicional Duelo de Coco de Roda do Rogério Dias e o Samba da Periferia;

Sábado (21): Pagode do Rafinha e da banda Vibrações;

Domingo (22): Naná Martins e show do Ilê Aiyê.

Espaço dedicado à literatura e artes, que recebe as autoras Cida Bento (O Pacto da Branquitude) e Carla Akotirene (Interseccionalidade), além de saraus, rodas de samba, performances teatrais e o pocket show de Tiganá Santana.

Recreação e oficinas gratuitas para o público infantil.

O espaço é dedicado à tecnologia, à inovação e à cultura digital, permitindo vivências imersivas em realidade virtual.

articles.title: Áudios de live de Marília Mendonça em 2021 geram mais um álbum póstumo da cantora, falecida há cinco anos | G1
articles.body:
Imagem de Marília Mendonça (1995 – 2021) na capa do álbum póstumo 'Manuscritos – Capítulo II' — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Desde que Marília Mendonça (22 de julho de 1995 – 5 de novembro de 2021) morreu em acidente de avião, há cinco anos, a discografia da cantora e compositora vem sendo expandida com singles, EPs e álbuns póstumos, alguns de caráter redundante.

A partir das 21h de hoje, quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, mais um título será agregado à obra fonográfica da artista. Com 12 músicas, sendo que seis dessas 12 faixas já tinham sido apresentadas em abril no EP “Manuscritos – Capítulo I” (2026), o álbum “Manuscritos – Capítulo II” rebobina registros de live transmitida por Marília Mendonça em 2021, durante o isolamento social imposto pela pandemia de covid-19.

O álbum será promovido com foco na faixa “No dia do seu casamento”, parceria de Marília com Juliano Tchula e Maraísa lançada em outubro de 2013 pela dupla Maiara & Maraisa como primeiro single do álbum também intitulado “No dia do seu casamento” e editado em 2014.

Músicas como “A voz do coração” (Marília Mendonça, Juliano Tchula e Maraisa, 2015) e “4 e 15” (Marília Mendonça, Vine Show, Juliano Tchula e Junior Gomes, 2015) também integram o repertório de “Manuscritos – Capítulo II”.

Convém ressaltar, no entanto, que a rigor quase todas as músicas desse álbum originado dos áudios da live da cantora também podem ser ouvidas no recente álbum lançado em 16 de outubro com a trilha sonora original da série documental “Marília Mendonça – Sentimento louco” (2026), disponível na plataforma de streaming Prime Video.

articles.title: 'Ramayana' box office collection Day 14: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash starrer crosses Rs 1,000 crore in India; hits Rs 1,500 crore globally in record time
articles.summary: Namit Malhotra's 'Ramayana', directed by Nitesh Tiwari has hit another historic milestone in record time at the Indian box office.
articles.body: Namit Malhotra's 'Ramayana', directed by Nitesh Tiwari has hit another historic milestone in record time at the Indian box office.In just two weeks of its theatrical run, the film has officially crossed the Rs 1,000 crore mark in the domestic market. As reported by Sacnilk, the epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, has become the sixth Indian film and the third Hindi production to enter the coveted club. The achievement also marks the first time that Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi have had a film cross the Rs 1,000 Crore India gross milestone.Ramayana Movie Review'Ramayana' Day 14 collectionsAccording to the box office report, 'Ramayana' collected Rs 23.20 crore net across 22,289 shows on Day 14, taking its total India net collection to Rs 844.40 crore, while its cumulative domestic gross collection has now hit an estimated Rs 1,009.05 crore.'Ramayana' collections across languagesThe film's Hindi version contributed the largest share on its second Thursday, raking in an estimated Rs 16.50 crore from 17,661 shows. The Malayalam version, on the other hand, earned an estimated Rs 2.15 crore from 1,051 shows, while the Kannada dubbed version collected Rs 1.65 crore from 897 shows. The Tamil and Telugu versions contributed Rs 1.60 crore and Rs 1.30 crore, respectively.The film's all-language India net collection stands at an estimated Rs 23.20 crore. As per the report, this is an 18.9% decline from its Day 13 collection of Rs 28.60 crore.'Ramayana' worldwide box office collection crosses Rs 1,500 croreOverseas, the film collected Rs 8 crore on Day 14, thus taking its overseas gross collection to Rs 510 crore.With the domestic gross standing at Rs 1,009.05 crore, the film's worldwide gross collection has now officially hit a total of Rs 1,519.05 crore.'Ramayana' beats 'Dhurandhar' to hit Rs 1,500 crore mark in record time'Ramayana' managed to cross the milestone in just two weeks, faster than any other film that hit the mark. Previously, 'Dhurandhar' held the record, which it achieved in approximately 3 weeks of its release.'Ramayana' becomes third Bollywood film to enter Rs 1,000 crore clubWhile crossing Rs 1,000 crore worldwide has become increasingly common for major Indian blockbusters, 'Ramayana' has joined an exclusive list that includes 'Baahubali 2', 'KGF: Chapter 2', 'Pushpa 2: The Rule' and the 'Dhurandhar' franchise.The film has also become only the third Bollywood movie to cross this milestone after Ranveer Singh's 'Dhurandhar' and 'Dhurandhar The Revenge' becoming the first Hindi films to enter the Rs 1,000 crore India gross club.The achievement also adds another milestone to Yash's box office record, with the actor now having two films in the exclusive club, following the success of 'KGF: Chapter 2'.'Ramayana' records strong international numbers'Ramayana', recorded openings of USD 573,000 (Rs 5.4 crore) in Indonesia and USD 286,000 (Rs 2.7 crore) in Cambodia, which the makers said were records for an Indian film in those markets. It also registered a record opening in Mexico.Among its leading international markets, the film has earned USD 24 million (Rs 225.6 crore) in the US and Canada, USD 5.5 million (Rs 51.7 crore) in the UK, USD 4.7 million (Rs 44.2 crore) in the UAE, USD 4.2 million (Rs 39.5 crore) in Australia, USD 1.5 million (Rs 14.1 crore) in Thailand, USD 1.4 million (Rs 13.2 crore) in Malaysia and USD 1.1 million (Rs 10.3 crore) in Germany.The film is scheduled to release in Brazil, Italy, Ukraine and Hungary on November 19, followed by Poland on November 20. articles.title: Watching sex comedy 'The Invite' with your spouse may lead to divorce, per Penélope Cruz
articles.summary: Since-divorced fans of 'The Invite' have reached out to the cast of the sex comedy to thank them for ending their marriages.
articles.body:
The sex comedy " The Invite " may be the perfect date night movie for some couples, and a litmus test for others.

The film stars Olivia Wilde and Seth Rogen as a couple whose marriage is on the rocks. They're both unfulfilled in their careers, and their relationship is marked by an underlying malaise and lack of intimacy. Enter the noisy couple upstairs, a retired firefighter and widow played by Edward Norton and a sexologist played by Penélope Cruz . The four get together for a dinner party and things go awry when it's revealed that all that ruckus upstairs comes from regular sex parties, and the couple in question likes to swing.

The movie's been a critical and commercial hit, and the talk of the town with Oscars campaigning underway. But Cruz said the stars of the film are also hearing from audiences that the film hit a nerve, so much so that some couples are calling it quits.

"Some people even write to us to tell us that they are thanking us for their divorce, which the movie, I think, is very honest and it can bring up conversations that are necessary," Cruz told People on Monday.

"And some people are telling us, 'Oh, thank you. This actually helped us to solve a problem in the relationship,' and some people are thanking us straight for their divorce."

Edward Norton told the Guardian that audiences are similarly gushing to him about the movie, "People are almost tearful. They're like: 'I haven't had a good, adult laugh that made me feel seen in a long time.'"

"Most people feel alone inside the dysfunction of their relationship — worried it's only the two of you having these problems. Universality is a relief. It lets you forgive yourself a lot."

According to Wilde, who directed the film, it's a terribly common issue in American marriages that after the couple welcomes a child, their sex life becomes deprioritized and the yearning for more becomes taboo. "It's that American sense of duty: I have begun this marriage, I will complete it, I will muscle through," she told the Guardian.

"The puritanical roots of our culture mean it's not only shameful to value pleasure, but also to admit defeat.... Pleasure and your continuing exploration of it is secondary to keeping the family unit intact."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Ella Langley dominates CMA Awards with major wins as Taylor Swift makes stunning return to stage
articles.summary: Ella Langley dominates the CMAs as she wins big while Taylor Swift makes her return after decade-long absence.
articles.body: The 60th annual Country Music Association Awards took place live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday night. Ella Langley dominated the awards ceremony, as the winner of entertainer of the year, the biggest award of the night. While accepting the award, she joked that the crowd must be sick of her already, getting a laugh from those in the room. "This isn't real life," she said while accepting the award. "Thank you Jesus, I'm at a loss for words," she added, before saying, "This has been the most special night. As she swept all the categories she was nominated in, Lainey Wilson brought out a bedazzled broom for her, telling her she knew she had it prepared as she knew Langley was going to sweep the show. Langley also won music video of the year before the broadcast. "Choosin' Texas" was named as the music video of the year winner during Good Morning America Wednesday morning. The record-breaking hit, also won single of the year and song of the year. Later in the show, Langley got teary-eyed as she accepted the award for album of the year, for her album, "Dandelion," noting it took two years to make. She was speechless while accepting the award and received a standing ovation from the audience. "I’m at a loss for words. I don’t know what to say," she said in her speech. "I love country music and I love what I do." Her wins also resulted in two wins for Miranda Lambert, who is credited as a producer on the song. Langley continued her winning streak later on in the show when she took home the award for female vocalist of the year, beating out Lambert, Musgraves, Moroney and Wilson for the honor. "I have so much love and respect for every single person and every single woman in this category," she said while accepting the award. "This is what I have lived and breathed not only just the past seven years that I moved to Nashville, but genuinely my whole entire life. I haven’t wanted to do another thing. There wasn’t anything on my heart. I never had a plan B. I was never gonna have a plan b. If I was still playing cover gigs with a tip jar out in front of me for four hours I’d still be doing this." Rising star Langley led the pack with 9 nominations, tying Lainey Wilson and Lambert's all-time record for the most nods by a female artist in a single year. Her win for single of the year left Taylor Swift going home empty-handed tonight, which didn't stop Taylor Swift from cheering for her as she went up to accept the award. Swift made her big return to the CMA Awards – after last attending in 2016. Her single, "I Knew It, I Knew You," is nominated for single of the year. The singer took the stage to perform at the CMA Awards for the first time in 13 years, starting her performance with her nominated song, before transitioning into one of her classic hits, "Our Song." Lambert also had a moment on stage with Kacey Musgraves, when the two sang their hit duet, "Horses and Divorces," from Musgraves' latest album, "Middle of Nowhere." The song references the rumored feud between the two singers, with them patching things up earlier this year. Zach Top honored veteran and military families, bringing one on stage and surprising them with the return of their son from service. In addition to her performance with Musgraves, Lambert took the stage once again with Langley to sing their song, "Snakeskin Boots" for the first time on television. The two matched in their versions of brown dresses with snakeskin print and fringe as they commanded the stage during their performance. Brooks and Dunn won vocal duo of the year for the 17th time in a row at this year’s award show. In addition, the duo also received the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award, which was presented to them by Swift. Prior to Swift handing them the award, Luke Bryan took to the stage alongside Brothers Osborne, HARDY, Marcus King, and Halestorm to pay tribute to the iconic duo. Little Big Town announced Chris Stapleton as the winner of male vocalist of the year. The musician took the stage earlier in the evening with both Mumford & Sons to sing "Here" and Stephen Wilson Jr. to sing, "I’m a Song." During his speech he encouraged fans to follow their dreams, and dedicated the award to his mother, who died last year around this time. "She always told me that I could be whatever I wanted to be, and turns out that was true," he said. Lady A introduced Tim McGraw to the stage to perform, "Don’t Take the Girl" for the first time on the CMA stage, as he is one of the Country Music Hall of Fame inductees this year. It was an intimate performance with the majority of the stage lights turned off save for a few spotlights behind him. Wilson returned to host the event for the third consecutive time, her second solo. Wilson is also nominated for entertainer of the year, which she won in 2023 and 2025. She also took to the stage during the show to perform her hit song, "Just A Woman." Megan Moroney blew fans away while strumming on her pink guitar as she sang "Beautiful Things" into her pink microphone. During her performance, fans surrounding the stage held up pink roses, while everyone in the arena swayed to the beat as with their flashlights lighting up the crowd. Tucker Wetmore got the crowd pumped with his performance of "Who Told You That," encouraging the crowd to get up and dance. While singing he enthusiastically played the piano which was surrounded by a circle of fire on the stage. The show began with a tribute to Dolly Parton. Parton was one of the most decorated figures in CMA Awards history, earning 45 nominations and winning 10 trophies over her career, including entertainer of the year in 1978, two female vocalist of the year awards, and the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016. Beyond her wins, she also helped define the telecast itself, famously co-hosting the ceremony in 1988 and returning in 2019 to co-host alongside Carrie Underwood and Reba McEntire. articles.title: Larry Poindexter, “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital” actor, dies at 66 after being hit by car: Report
articles.summary: The veteran actor also appeared in “S.W.A.T.,” “17 Again,” “Friends,” “JAG,” and dozens of other projects.
articles.body:
Veteran actor Larry Poindexter died on Nov. 18 at age 66.

Deadline reported that he was struck by a car days earlier in Studio City, Calif.

Poindexter had two stints on Days of Our Lives among his dozens of TV credits.

Larry Poindexter, the character actor best known for stints on soap operas like Days of Our Lives and General Hospital , has died. He was 66.

Deadline reported that Poindexter died on Wednesday, days after being struck by a car while crossing the street in his Studio City neighborhood. The actor was reportedly at the hospital and scheduled to undergo surgery for broken ribs when he died suddenly.

Entertainment Weekly has reached out to representatives for Poindexter for more information.

Poindexter was born in Dallas in 1959 to H.R. Poindexter, a Tony Award-winning light and set designer, and Sue Ann Erdman, an opera singer. He made his stage debut in Dallas Summer Musicals, where his parents first met, and received his first TV credit for a 1982 episode of A New Day in Eden . His first screen acting project, the TV movie Thursday's Child , premiered a year later and starred Rob Lowe, Gena Rowlands, and Jessica Walter.

Poindexter said that he landed the role by accident after interrupting a casting session for the TV movie while dropping off paperwork for the producer he worked for at the time.

"I had just walked out, and the door flies open and she strides up to me and asks; 'Are you an actor?" he recalled on his website . "I say; 'Yes.' 2 weeks later I auditioned for a part in the movie I was a production assistant on - and got it!"

Poindexter's first soap stint came when he played Ben Welch on eight episodes of Days of Our Lives in 1984. The actor appeared on individual episodes of shows like Happy Days , CHiPs , Silver Spoons , and Growing Pains throughout the 1980s before his 23-episode stint as Justin Moore on Santa Barbara in 1986.

He went on to appear on seven episodes of Duet and a pair of Quantum Leap episodes in the late '80s, and also acted in movies like Number One With a Bullet , Blue Movies , and Invaders From Mars .

In the '90s, Poindexter appeared in all 22 episodes of Fox's Too Something , also known as New York Daze , and played Dalton Lowne on seven episodes of JAG . He also acted in episodes of Friends , Lois & Clark: The New Adventures of Superman , ALF , Party of Five , and Murphy Brown .

Poindexter played Dr. Asher Thomas on 12 episodes of General Hospital in 2005. He acted on several prominent series throughout the 2000s including CSI , Will & Grace , Nip/Tuck , Weeds , and Bones . He also acted opposite Samuel L. Jackson and Colin Farrell in 2003's S.W.A.T. , and played small supporting role in 17 Again .

The actor appeared on almost every episode of MTV's The Hard Times of RJ Berger , which ran from 2010 to 2011, and returned to Days of Our Lives to play a different character, the priest Father Louis. He also performed in episodes of The Mentalist , Scandal , Castle , Hawaii Five-0 , K.C. Undercover , and NCIS .

In the 2020s, Poindexter appeared on three eps of Station 19 and guest starred on Curb Your Enthusiasm , 9-1-1 , The Lincoln Lawyer , and The Rookie .

Poindexter also acted and produced for the stage throughout his career, performing in productions of Fatherland , In the Valley of the Shadow , Boys in the Band , The Night of the Iguana , and Tender Is the Night . He produced and developed Broadway's The Cher Show , which won two Tonys in 2019.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

In addition to acting and producing, Poindexter sang lead in an alt-country band called The High Lonesome, which released the album Feel Free To Do So in 1995.

Poindexter is survived by his wife, casting director Carol Kritzer, and their twin sons.

articles.title: Ella Langley sweeps 2026 CMA Awards, wins entertainer of the year
articles.summary: It didn’t take a crystal ball to see: The 2026 Country Music Association Awards were always going to be all about Ella Langley.
articles.body: It didn’t take a crystal ball to see: The 2026 Country Music Association Awards were always going to be all about Ella Langley. The Alabama-born-and-raised singer was named entertainer of the year during Wednesday’s event — beating the host of the evening and last year’s winner Lainey Wilson, as well as Cody Johnson, Luke Combs and Chris Stapleton, for the top prize. “At this point, I’m sick of me,” she started her acceptance speech with a joke, after having spent so much of the show on stage. “I could quit tomorrow and have the best career of my life.” Wilson emerged with a bedazzled broom because, “I told you, you was going to sweep, girl!” she said as she embraced Langley. It really was Langley’s night from the jump. The 60th annual CMA Awards, broadcast live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena, started and ended with her. Langley accepted the first award of the night, single of the year, for her history-making “Choosin’ Texas.” Competition was fierce: Taylor Swift’s song for the “Toy Story 5” film, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” was also nominated in the category, as were Langley’s own “Be Her,” Wilson’s “Somewhere Over Laredo” and Johnson’s “The Fall.” And then Langley was back on stage almost immediately afterward — to perform her joyous “Loving Life Again” with a string quartet and to pick up another award, when “Choosin’ Texas” was named song of the year. “This song is the gift that keeps on giving,” she said in her speech. She also won female vocalist as well as album of the year, the latter for her thrilling, old-soul country “Dandelion.” “My lip is already quivering,” she said. “I’m at a loss for words.” The return of Taylor Swift and a tribute to Dolly Parton Swift was also in the building. The pop powerhouse lit up the CMA Awards by performing “I Knew It, I Knew You” with a bit of her 2006 country hit “Our Song” mixed in for good measure. She began her set in the back halls of the arena before hitting the stage — joined by Keith Urban on banjo, no less — as if no time had passed. But it’s been 13 years since Swift last performed at the CMA Awards, a decade after her last appearance there and 17 years after being named the youngest entertainer of the year in the show’s history. Consider it a treat in a night full of them. The show began with a powerful tribute to the larger-than-life Dolly Parton. The American icon died in August at age 80, and her legacy will be felt for many decades to come. Host Wilson got the celebration started, duetting Parton’s “I Will Always Love You” with the legendary singer-songwriter Vince Gill. Then she was joined by singer Brad Paisley in a funny opening monologue where the pair sang modern parodies of famous country songs: Loretta Lynn’s “Coal Miner’s Daughter” became “Data Miner’s Daughter,” and Willie Nelson’s “Always On My Mind” was transformed into “Always On My Phone.” No shortage of awards and performances here A standout set arrived early: Kacey Musgraves and Miranda Lambert duetted “Horses & Divorces” — a song from Musgraves’ latest album, “Middle of Nowhere,” that doubles as a delicious resolution from the pair of former frenemies — with its norteño accordion and shout-along lyrics. The stage was set to look like an ’80s beauty parlor, recalling one of Parton’s most famous acting roles: the 1989 film “Steel Magnolias.” Tim McGraw brought it back to the ’90s, singing “Don’t Take the Girl.” Megan Moroney slowed things down with her big-hearted ballad “Beautiful Things.” Tucker Wetmore was joined by a brass band for a bit of his single “Who Told You That” before launching into some of Hank Williams Jr.’s 1984 hit “All My Rowdy Friends Are Coming Over Tonight.” Combs tackled his song “Miss You Here.” Lambert and Langley brought some country-disco with “Snakeskin Boots.” Mumford & Sons teamed up with Stapleton for “Here.” Later, Stapleton would hop back on stage to join Stephen Wilson Jr. — and to be awarded male vocalist of the year, for a ninth time in his career. Lainey Wilson performed a brand new one, the full-throated “Just A Woman.” It was a bit of a theme: The modern traditionalist Zach Top also debuted a new track, the bluegrass-y “Moonshine.” Before he left the stage, Dierks Bentley joined in for a tribute to the late John Anderson. They sang his 1983 single “Swingin’.” Best new artist went to Stephen Wilson Jr.; vocal group went for a second year in a row to the Red Clay Strays, who also performed their song “Revival.” Brooks & Dunn took home vocal duo for the 17th time. “I love to hear myself talk, and I’ve actually run out of things to say,” Kix Brooks said in his acceptance speech. “Thanks for making us famous.” “Follow the yellow brick road,” added Ronnie Dunn. Later in the night, they received the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award. Halestorm, Marcus King, Brothers Osborne, Hardy and Luke Bryan paid tribute to the legendary country music duo, covering some of their biggest hits: “Boot Scootin’ Boogie,” “Rock My World (Little Country Girl),” “Hard Workin’ Man,” “Hillbilly Deluxe” and “Play Something Country.” Prizes are nominated and voted on by members of the Country Music Association, which includes music executives, artists, publicists, songwriters and other industry professionals.

articles.title: Islam expected to surpass Christianity as world’s largest religion by 2035
articles.summary: Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s largest religion by 2035, according to detailed projections released by the Pew Research Center.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s largest religion by 2035, according to detailed projections released Wednesday by the Pew Research Center. Pew, which has been issuing authoritative reports on religious demography for 25 years, said both Islam and Christianity are growing, but Islam is growing much faster. A key reason, Pew said, is that Muslims tend to have more children than other major religious groups. “It’s the babies,” said Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett, explaining that conversion and other ways of changing religious identity are much smaller factors than fertility rates. During 2020-2025, the fertility rate for Muslims was 3.1 children per woman, followed by the rate for Christians at 2.5, according to Pew. The average fertility rate for all other women was 1.6, below the level of 2.1 that’s considered necessary for each generation to replace itself. According to Pew’s latest estimates, there were 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims worldwide in 2020. Pew’s new projections forecast that there will be 2.57 billion Muslims and 2.52 billion Christians by 2035. By 2070, if recent trends continue, there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under 3 billion Christians worldwide. The estimates are part of a broader Pew project examining how the size of major religious groups could change between 2020 and 2070. The projections take into account recent differences between religious groups’ age profiles, fertility rates, and patterns of religious switching and migration. Among the many notable findings: Pew projects that the United States, within 40 years, will no longer have a Christian majority. Christians now account for 62% of U.S. adults, according to Pew, and will fall below 50% by 2065. In neighboring Canada, Christians are expected to drop below 50% by 2030, Pew said. In both countries, a significant reason for the drop is the concurrent increase in the number of people with no religious affiliation. By 2070, they are projected to account for 41% of the U.S. population and to outnumber Christians in Canada. Muslims and Christians are expected to keep pace with population growth The world’s population is projected to increase by 29% between 2020 and 2070, Pew said. Of the religious groups it analyzed, Muslims and Christians are the only ones expected to keep pace, with Christians growing by 30% and Muslims by 80%. Although Hindus and Jews are growing in absolute numbers, they are projected to decline as a percentage of the global population, Pew said. It forecasts that Buddhists would shrink both in number and as a portion of the world’s population, in part due to expected declines in the overall populations of China, South Korea and Japan. Over the coming decades, Pew said, most of the world’s population growth is expected to occur in Africa, particularly south of the Sahara Desert, where most people are Christians or Muslims. The region’s high fertility and rising life expectancy will boost the global numbers of both faiths, Pew predicted. By 2070, Pew said, more than half of the world’s Christians will live in sub-Saharan Africa, and Congo will surpass the United States as the country with the most Christians, with their ranks increasing more than threefold to 299 million. The populations of other major regions are expected to grow more modestly, or even decline. For example, the number of people living in Europe will shrink by 17% by 2070, Pew said, and the number of Christians there will drop by a third, from 505 million to 324 million. Over the same period, the percentage of Europe’s population that is Muslim is expected to increase from 6% to 13%. In the U.S., Pew projects that the number of Christians will decline from about 217 million in 2020 to about 174 million in 2070. Several mainline Protestant denominations in the U.S. have faced declining membership over many years. However, Jeffrey Brodd, a religious studies professor at California State-Sacramento, suggested a rebound was possible following congressional election victories this month by several Democrats active in these moderate-to-liberal denominations. Fertility rates are a driving factor By Pew’s estimates, Muslim women gave birth to more babies than women in any other religion during 2020-2025. About 252 million babies were born to Muslim mothers, compared with 208 million born to Christian mothers. Muslims are the only major religious group expected to have growing numbers of births in the decades ahead. The other groups are projected either to have steady numbers of births or to experience gradual decline. If recent trends continue, according to Pew, Pakistan will have the largest Muslim population by 2070, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia — which currently has the most Muslims. Gina Zurlo, a senior researcher at Harvard Divinity School specializing in religious demographics, said Christian-Muslim relations are “extremely important” in light of the evolving trends. “The ‘clash of civilization’ theory still looms large in some religious communities and there is a lot of misunderstanding of both religions from both sides,” she said via email. “Many Christians are not happy to see that Islam will be the world’s largest religion and it’s causing even more angst.” “I hope people seek opportunities for greater interreligious education,” she added. “Personal contact is important — when people have personal relationships across religious differences, it ‘humanizes’ the ‘other’ in fruitful ways.” Alan Cooperman, Pew’s director of religion research, noted that most of the projected proliferation of Muslims and Christians was occurring in countries where they already are the majority — with conversion playing only a minor role. “I don’t think this is a situation in which the growth of Muslims is coming at the expense of Christians,” he added. “I do worry about mischief being made with headlines or narratives that take this finding and portray it as sort of a clash where Christians are losing to Muslims.” The ‘nones’ are growing in some areas Many countries have seen a steady proliferation of the “nones” — people who are atheist, agnostic or religiously unaffiliated. Excluding China, which has a high proportion of “nones” but faces a sharp decline in overall population, the ranks of “nones” elsewhere will grow by more than 180 million by 2070, Pew said. The “nones” already account for a majority of the population in 10 countries, including the Czech Republic, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Uruguay and Vietnam, according to Pew. South Korea, France and the United Kingdom are forecast to join this group by 2070.

articles.standfirst: Un filme francés que dirige Tristan Séguéla
articles.summary: Un filme francés que dirige Tristan Séguéla
articles.body: Las plataformas de streaming han encontrado en los dramas judiciales uno de sus principales baluartes y atractivos de cara a obtener buenos números de visualizaciones. Netflix es el mayor exponente de este tipo de producciones, bien sea a través de series o películas. En esta ocasión, el gigante estadounidense ha querido estrenar una cinta de origen francés que se ha colado rápidamente en el top-3 de lo más visto en España. Hablamos de ‘Un buen abogado’, un drama estrenado el pasado 9 de noviembre y que dirige el cineasta Tristan Séguéla, quien también firma el guion junto a Simon Jacquet y Marcia Romano. A lo largo de sus 114 minutos, la película pone a prueba los límites morales y la búsqueda de la justicia cuando la integridad de uno mismo está en juego. “El abogado penalista Léonard Landry sufre una sobredosis en el juzgado. Tras pasar por rehabilitación, dispone de una semana para preparar su propio juicio con la ayuda de una obstinada becaria. Comienza así una frenética carrera de maniobras legales, tentaciones y giros inesperados”, dice su sinopsis en Filmaffinity. La película cuenta con un reparto de lujo en Francia que encabeza Laurent Lafitte, y a quien siguen: Anthony Bajon, Mélanie Laurent, Carole Bouquet, Vincent Cassel, Gedéon Ekay, Béatrice Facquer, Gwendal Kerdelhue, Patrice Mendes, Francisco Luzemo, Sonia Cougar, Marv Trim, entre otros. ‘Un buen abogado’ se estrenó primero en el Festival de Venecia, donde recibió buenas críticas y, tras el análisis de la prensa especializada, ha continuado con esa tendencia. “La película funciona mejor como un drama sobre los curiosos y no particularmente eficaces intentos de un abogado por redimirse y no perder su título que como thriller socioeconómico ligado al caso en el que se involucra”, expresa el experto Diego Lerer en MicropsiaCine.

articles.title: Saif Ali Khan gets death threat from accused in Baba Siddiqui's murder case: Report
articles.summary: After the gunfire incident on Tiger Shroff, Bollywood has been facing a series of death threats.
articles.body: After the gunfire incident on Tiger Shroff, Bollywood has been facing a series of death threats. Several celebrity names have surfaced and now as per a latest update Saif Ali Khan has got a death threat with the name of Zeeshan Akhtar, a wanted accused in the Baba Siddiqui murder case, emerging in connection with the threat. Mumbai Police is investigating the matter and is trying to ascertain whether Akhtar was actually behind the threat or if someone else used his name to target the actor and harass the authorities.Saif is the latest Bollywood actor to receive a threat, following similar incidents involving Tusshar Kapoor and Ayushmann Khurrana earlier this month. In those cases, police arrested Vaibhav Mishra, a 30-year-old IT graduate from Bengaluru. Investigators found that he had no links to any criminal gang and had allegedly used artificial intelligence to send the threatening messages.Police are now examining whether the latest threat was genuinely issued by Zeeshan Akhtar or whether an impersonator is using his identity to intimidate celebrities. Saif Ali Khan has not yet issued a statement regarding the matter.The threat comes nearly two years after Saif was attacked by an intruder at his Bandra residence on January 16, 2025. The incident took place around 2 am, when the intruder allegedly entered the actor's home and reached the room where Saif and Kareena Kapoor's younger son, Jeh, was sleeping.Saif reportedly confronted the intruder to protect his son but was stabbed multiple times during the altercation, sustaining serious injuries to his neck and back. He was subsequently rushed to Lilavati Hospital, where he underwent a six-hour surgery. The actor was discharged five days later.Recalling the terrifying aftermath of the attack, Kareena had spoken about the panic that gripped the family. articles.title: Westside Cowboy named BBC Introducing Artist of the Year 2026
articles.summary: The band follow previous winners including Olivia Dean, Myles Smith and Tom Grennan.
articles.body:
Westside Cowboy have been announced as BBC Introducing Artist of the Year 2026.

Jimmy Bradbury, Reuben Haycocks, Aoife Anson O'Connell and Paddy Murphy formed the band in Manchester in 2023 and have since rocketed from the pub circuit to some of the UK's biggest festivals.

The award is presented to an up-and-coming artist or band who has, with the support of BBC Introducing, made a significant impact and has previously been won by Olivia Dean, Myles Smith and Tom Grennan.

Murphy, from Longridge in Lancashire, said the win put them in "good company", with Bradbury, from Shropshire, adding that it was "very flattering".

BBC Introducing supports new musical talent across the UK , providing a platform to propel new artists on to the local and national stage through 30 Introducing shows, three national radio shows and six shows across BBC Radio 1, Radio 1Xtra, Radio 2, 6Music, Radio 3 and Asian Network.

About 72,000 tracks from emerging UK artists supported by BBC Introducing make it on to the airwaves each year.

Westside Cowboy uploaded their debut single I've Never Met Anyone I Thought I Could Really Love (Until I Met You) to the Introducing platform in November 2024 and had their first play on radio within hours.

The four-piece played in various other bands before coming together to form Westside Cowboy.

Haycocks, O'Connell, and Murphy had met at Manchester's Royal Northern College of Music in 2021 and later got to know Bradbury after meeting him in the nearby Johnny Roadhouse music shop.

Murphy and Bradbury played in surf-rock trio Katz, while Murphy and Haycocks both worked together in noise-pop trio, DieKaiDie, but it was when Bradbury, who was working in the music shop repairing guitars, asked the others if they wanted to start a new band that Westside Cowboy's journey began.

By the time their second single, Shells, was released in April 2025, they had been been selected to play the BBC Introducing stage at Glastonbury Festival, and the song was put on the BBC 6Music playlist.

Their meteoric rise saw seen them appear on BBC music show Later... with Jools Holland in June and their debut album It Goes On was released on Island Records in August, peaking at number five in the UK charts.

Thanking the Introducing network and listeners for their support, Murphy said it was "really cool to be recognised for the music you make".

"We say this a lot, so apologies if we sound like a broken record, [but] it's funny with this band because... we started it with so little pretence or plan," he said.

"So whenever people give us something cool like [this award], it's all a bit surreal because it still feels like a weekend project that we now just get to do way more regularly.

"We're very lucky it's one of those things.

William Wolstenholme, presenter and producer of BBC Introducing in Lancashire & Cumbria, gave the band their first play and said he remembers messaging them to upload the track.

"Over the past two years, Westside Cowboy have become surely the most exciting band in Manchester, and therefore the country," he said.

"They've fast-tracked from the sweaty pubs of the city's student music scene to many of the most famous venues in the country.

"It's a rise whose speed can scarcely be believed, and one that has shocked much of the music industry."

He said the band's obvious camaraderie was one of their main selling points.

"They're still the same four mates wandering down Oxford Road in Manchester, and the reason the music has resonated with so many people is because it's a true reflection of those four kids," he said.

"They've been themselves and, in doing so, have brought the fashion and style of the past 10 years of UK post-punk culture down to earth."

articles.body: Superstar Rajinikanth recently spent some time with his grandson Yathra during a family trip to Greece. His elder daughter, Aishwarya Rajinikanth, shared a picture of the two walking alongside each other on social media. She also posted another photograph featuring her younger son, Linga Raja, during the holiday.Rajinikanth poses with grandson YathraIn a picture shared by Aishwarya on her Instagram handle, Rajinikanth and Yathra are seen walking next to each other. The superstar wore a brown T-shirt, black trousers and a black sports cap, while Yathra opted for an all-white outfit. The photograph captured a warm moment between the grandfather and grandson.Aishwarya Rajinikanth shares another picture from GreeceIn another post, Aishwarya shared a photograph with her younger son, Linga Raja. The two are seen smiling together, with Linga placing his arm around his mother's shoulder. The picture was taken in front of an ancient Greek temple featuring rows of stone columns, with scaffolding visible on part of the structure.Yathra is the elder son of Aishwarya and actor Dhanush. He was born on October 10, 2006. The former couple also have a younger son, Linga Raja, who was born in 2010. He is forced to return to his old ways to protect his family and legacy. articles.title: ‘Yeh Prem Mol Liya’ actress Sharvari praises Alia Bhatt’s multitasking skills; says she balanced work and motherhood on ‘Alpha’ sets
articles.summary: Actress Sharvari Wagh opened up about her experience of working with Alia Bhatt in 'Alpha' and recalled how she watched the actress balance her
articles.body: Actress Sharvari Wagh opened up about her experience of working with Alia Bhatt in 'Alpha' and recalled how she watched the actress balance her professional commitments with motherhood.Sharvari, who will appear as a special guest on Kon Honar Crorepati, spoke to host Madhuri Dixit about her admiration for Alia and the experience of sharing screen space with her.Talking about Alia, Sharvari said, "Alia is my favourite actress. Especially because she is obviously a senior actor to me. The films she has done, the stories she has brought to the screen and the characters she has played have all been very inspiring. I have always felt that I want to do films like these. So, Alia has always been an inspiration. When I found out that we were doing a film together, I was extremely happy."Sharvari further recalled that she looked at the opportunity to work with Alia as a chance to learn from her. She said, "But more than that, I thought I would become a fly on the wall and learn everything I could from Alia. As a human being, she is outstanding. I remember that she herself looks so young, but she also has a little daughter. Even between shots, she is constantly planning things. She knows everything that is happening. During the takes, she is completely focused and gives her ten out of ten, while also managing things at home, her brands and everything else. She is a multitasker."Madhuri Dixit was also impressed by Alia's ability to manage her personal and professional responsibilities. Reacting to Sharvari's observation, Madhuri said, "Wow! That's wonderful. She is not just an actress but also someone who pays attention to everything in her life."For the uninitiated, Sharvari and Alia worked together in 'Alpha', the action-thriller directed by Shiv Rawail and part of Yash Raj Films' spy universe. articles.title: Liverpool sending scouts ‘every week’ to watch red-hot sensation in shock Golden Boot contention
articles.summary: According to reports from Italy, Liverpool are regularly scouting a red-hot striker who’s emerged as a shock candidate for the Golden Boot in Serie A this se...
articles.body:
According to reports from Italy, Liverpool are regularly scouting a red-hot striker who's emerged as a shock candidate for the Golden Boot in Serie A this season.

Andoni Iraola has been almost exclusively reliant on Alexander Isak at centre-forward since taking charge of the Reds in the summer, with Hugo Ekitike continuing his recovery from a long-term Achilles injury .

The Frenchman is targeting a return to action next month ( The Athletic ), although it appears that Anfield chiefs are keeping tabs on a positional alternative who's emerging as a breakthrough sensation in one of Europe's major leagues.

Liverpool heavily scouting Gustavo Varela

A report from Corriere dello Sport has claimed that Liverpool are sending scouts 'every week' to watch Gustavo Varela, who's been in remarkable goalscoring form with Monza since joining the Serie A outfit in the summer.

Napoli and Juventus have also been strongly linked with the 21-year-old, who's been the subject of enquiries from Tottenham, Brentford and Sunderland, with the list of suitors growing in tandem with his goal return in the Italian top flight.

Ivan Juric's side reportedly want €40m (£33.5m) for the Portuguese hitman, which'd represent a monumental profit on a player they signed from Gil Vicente in July for a paltry €2.5m (£2.1m).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Varela's rise to prominence has been extraordinary

Varela is currently the leading scorer in Serie A this season with nine goals, which is remarkable when his team are currently in the relegation zone, and he accounts for more than half of their goal tally in the top flight so far.

For someone who'd scored just seven times in 34 senior appearances before the summer, his form since joining Monza has been extraordinary. Should that continue, it's safe to say that he won't be at the Stadio Brianteo for much longer.

What Liverpool would need to consider is whether this is a mere purple patch from the Portuguese youngster, or the start of a journey towards being one of Europe's most feared centre-forwards.

Varela has scored nine Serie A goals from an xG of just 5.48 ( Fotmob ), an astonishing overperformance which begs the question as to whether he can maintain that for a full campaign.

If Isak keeps up his own hot streak and Ekitike gets back to the levels he'd shown prior to his injury, it'd be difficult to see the Monza striker getting much of a look-in at Anfield.

However, it's easy to see why Liverpool are routinely dispatching scouts to gather information on one of the breakout stars of European football in 2026.

articles.title: OTT releases this week (November 20-22): Find out where to watch Prashanth Neel-presented ‘418’, ‘Anbil Avan’, ‘Mr & Mrs Office’ and more
articles.summary: Multiple South Indian content is arriving on digital platforms this week across multiple genres including a mix of horror, romance, comedy and action.
articles.body: Multiple South Indian content is arriving on digital platforms this week across multiple genres including a mix of horror, romance, comedy and action. From a supernatural mystery presented by Prashanth Neel to a family entertainer starring Anupama Parameswaran, here are five titles to add to your weekend watchlist.‘418’Presented by ‘Salaar’ and ‘KGF’ filmmaker Prashanth Neel, 418 is a supernatural horror thriller set in a village. The story revolves around VIMS, an abandoned medical college building that has remained sealed for 15 years. When the building reopens despite opposition from locals, a series of unexplained incidents begins.The protagonist is a student who can sense supernatural occurrences, struggles to convince others about the danger. The film shows a sealed hostel storeroom “Room No. 418”. Directed by Kirtan Nadagouda, the film features Chaithra J Achar, Ramesh Indira, Surya Raj Veerabathini, Charan Lakkaraju, Preethi Pagadala and others.The film can be watched on Netflix.‘Mr & Mrs Office’‘Mr & Mrs Office’ is a Tamil workplace comedy web series about a married couple who work at the same IT company but decide to keep their relationship a secret from their colleagues. Their attempt to hide their marriage leads to a series of awkward and humorous situations at the workplace. Pradeep Antony and Smeha Manimegalai play the lead couple in the series.The series is available to watch on Jio Hotstar.‘Kiku Chiranjeevi’The Telugu film follows Chiru, a young orphan who hopes to create a better future for himself. His life takes an unexpected turn when he falls in love with Manasa, who sets several conditions before agreeing to marry him. Just when Chiru starts dreaming of a happy life together, he faces an unexpected fight for survival. The film also stars Kiku Yanamala, Kashish Khan, Easwari Rao and Tanikella Bharani. It streams on JioHotstar.‘Anbil Avan’‘Anbil Avan’ is a Tamil romantic action thriller directed by R Kaarthikeyan. The film stars Ashok Selvan and Preity Mukhundhan as Suriya and Iyal, a couple who fall in love, get married and decide to begin a new chapter of their lives in a hill station.However, their fresh start takes an unexpected turn as the story moves into darker territory. Revathi, Sabumon Abdusamad, Kadirbalu and Maha Delhi Ganesh also play key roles. Govind Vasantha has composed the music. Watch it on Sony LIV.‘Crazy Kalyanam’‘Crazy Kalyanam’ revolves around Parvathalu, a family man who is worried about the social embarrassment caused by his elder daughter's troubled marriage. Hoping to ensure a secure future for his younger daughter Keerthi, he arranges her marriage to a wealthy groom. However, Keerthi is secretly in love with her childhood friend Uday, a handloom weaver.Her confession just before the wedding turns the family’s plans upside down, resulting in a series of comic twists and unexpected situations. The film features Anupama Parameswaran, Tharun Bhascker Dhaassyam, Vijaya Krishna Naresh, Akhil Raj Uddemari, Chaitanya Madadi and Harsha Vardhan.The film will be available on Aha Video.'Cult'Vishwak Sen’s Telugu psychological thriller ‘Cult’, which was released in theatres on October 30, is now heading for its digital premiere. Written and directed by the actor, the film revolves around a birthday celebration that turns into a deadly nightmare following a series of killings. It includes Gayatri Bharadwaj, Tarak Ponnappa, Murali Sharma, Srikanth Iyengar and Prajna in key roles.
